newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen firm in short term.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen firm in short term.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to remain firm in the short term, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its weekly market preview.
This week's offering is 17,329 bales larger than originally rostered with a total offering of 72,199 bales in Sydney and Melbourne, it said.
In Sydney there are 29,329 bales, similar in selection to last week's with mainly good topmaking style Western New South Wales clips.
In Melbourne there are now 42,870 bales of good to best topmaking style with slightly higher vegetable matter content.
Last week's eastern market indicator rose 19 cents to 678 cents per kg clean, while the western indicator rose 29 cents to 631 cents, compared with sales in Fremantle two weeks ago.
Wesfarmers said with the firmer market, previously withheld stocks both on farm and in store have been attracted to auction and have increased this week's offering.

"This is expected to have a dampening effect on the market strength we have recently seen. However, due to the squeeze situation buyers are currently faced with, the dampening effect is not anticipated to be great and the market is expected to remain firm in the short term," Wesfarmers said.
